summary:
Survive on Moon is an educational survival game developed by Team TAY to make space science engaging, interactive, and accessible to young learners.

The game follows the story of an astronaut crew stranded on the Moon after a spacecraft crash. Players must explore the lunar environment, collect resources, craft equipment, build a lunar base, and repair their spacecraft to return home. Throughout the journey, they must manage essential survival needs, including oxygen, water, food, temperature, and radiation exposure.

Our project addresses the challenge of making STEM education more engaging by combining scientific knowledge with storytelling, exploration, and survival mechanics. The game incorporates real NASA data and scientifically inspired lunar survival systems, allowing players to learn how astronauts would actually survive in the Moon's extreme environment.

Why is it important? Instead of simply reading about space, children experience its challenges firsthand. By turning education into an interactive adventure, Survive on Moon encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and an interest in science, technology, engineering, and space exploration.

Project Details — Survive on Moon

Team TAY | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. Project Overview and How It Works

Survive on Moon is an educational 3D survival game developed by Team TAY to make space science more engaging, interactive, and accessible to children aged 7–12 and more.

The game follows the story of an international astronaut crew travelling to the Moon. However, their spacecraft crashes, leaving them stranded on the lunar surface. Players must work together to survive, explore the environment, collect resources, construct their lunar base, and find a way to repair their spacecraft and return home.

Throughout the game, players can control different crew members, assign them tasks, explore lunar craters, operate a lunar rover, collect materials, and manage an inventory. They must also maintain essential survival systems to keep their crew alive.

2. Survival Needs and Resource Management

One of the core mechanics of our game is a survival needs system. Astronauts have several essential needs, including oxygen, water, food, temperature regulation, and radiation protection.

Each need must be continuously monitored and maintained. However, fulfilling these needs requires specific materials and resources. Players must explore the lunar environment, collect materials, and use them to produce essential supplies and maintain their survival systems.

For example, players must understand how oxygen can be generated, how water can be obtained and processed, and what resources are necessary to support human life in the lunar environment.

To develop these mechanics, we researched real space technologies and scientific approaches to producing oxygen, obtaining water, and maintaining life-support systems beyond Earth. We wanted our gameplay to reflect the actual engineering challenges involved in establishing a sustainable lunar outpost.

Characters can die if their essential needs are neglected, but they can respawn without losing their overall progress, allowing children to learn through experimentation and continue their mission.

3. Scientific Research and NASA Data

Scientific accuracy was one of our main priorities during development.

We researched NASA resources and scientific information concerning lunar surface conditions, extreme temperatures, radiation exposure, available resources, and the Moon's environment. We also explored information from NASA's Artemis program and other space exploration missions.

This research influenced our survival mechanics and the environmental conditions represented in the game. We wanted children to understand that surviving on the Moon is not simply about finding shelter but requires complex systems, careful resource management, and an understanding of the lunar environment.

Our goal was to connect educational gameplay with real scientific knowledge and introduce young players to the technologies and challenges involved in future lunar exploration.

4. Educational Cards and Interactive Learning

We introduced an educational card system directly into the game to help children understand the scientific concepts behind different activities and survival mechanics.

These cards provide accessible explanations about lunar conditions, resources, survival technologies, and space exploration. Instead of interrupting gameplay with long scientific explanations, we integrated learning materials into the experience.

This means that when children encounter different objects, resources, or survival challenges, they can also discover the science behind them.

We believe this approach makes learning more natural and memorable because children understand not only what they need to do but also why it matters.

5. Diversity and Inclusivity

We also focused on diversity and representation when designing our characters.

Our game features astronauts of different nationalities, genders, and cultural backgrounds, reflecting the international nature of real-world space exploration.

We believe space exploration should be represented as a collective human achievement, where people from different countries and backgrounds work together toward a common goal.

By introducing a diverse crew, we aim to promote inclusivity, cultural awareness, equality, and international collaboration. We also want children to see that science and space exploration are open to everyone, regardless of their gender or background.

6. User Interface and Accessibility

Since our primary target audience is children aged 7–12, we placed particular emphasis on creating a clear, intuitive, and user-friendly interface.

We carefully considered how information is presented, how players navigate between different systems, and how they monitor their astronauts' needs and available resources.

Our intention was to represent the complexity of lunar survival without making the gameplay unnecessarily complicated. We wanted every mechanic, resource indicator, and interaction to be understandable, even for children with little previous knowledge of space science.

Throughout development, we tried to consider every important detail while maintaining a balance between scientific accuracy, gameplay depth, accessibility, and simplicity.

Our philosophy was to make the underlying science realistic while keeping the overall experience enjoyable and easy to understand.

7. Creativity and Innovation

The main creative aspect of Survive on Moon is the combination of storytelling, scientific research, survival mechanics, and interactive education.

Rather than presenting isolated scientific facts, we place players inside a fictional lunar emergency where every action has a purpose.

The storyline gives children a reason to continue exploring, while survival mechanics encourage them to apply scientific knowledge to solve practical problems.

Another important feature is our crew management system. Players can control different astronauts and coordinate their activities, creating an experience that goes beyond traditional single-character survival games.

We also combine resource collection, crafting, lunar exploration, and educational cards to create an environment where learning happens naturally through gameplay.

Our aim was to make children feel like real astronauts rather than passive learners.

8. Educational Benefits and Intended Impact

Survive on Moon aims to introduce children to important STEM concepts through an engaging and interactive experience.

By playing the game, children can develop:

  • Space Science: Understanding the Moon's environment, surface conditions, temperature, and radiation.
  • Physics and Engineering: Discovering how oxygen generation, resource processing, and life-support technologies work.
  • Resource Management: Learning why resources are limited and why materials are essential for survival.
  • Critical Thinking: Making decisions and understanding the consequences of their actions.
  • Problem-Solving: Developing strategies to overcome unexpected challenges.
  • Teamwork and Collaboration: Coordinating astronauts and distributing responsibilities.
  • Scientific Curiosity: Developing an interest in space exploration, engineering, and future space missions.

Our intended impact is to make complex scientific concepts easier to understand and inspire children to become more interested in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

We want children to realize that space exploration is not only about rockets and astronauts but also about research, engineering, teamwork, and solving real-world problems.

9. Tools and Technologies

We used the following technologies and software to develop our project:

  • Unity: Main game engine used to develop the 3D game environment and gameplay systems.
  • C#: Programming language used to implement game mechanics, interactions, and survival systems.
  • Blender: Used for 3D modeling and asset creation.
  • GitHub: Used for version control and collaboration between team members.
  • Visual Studio Code: Used for writing and editing code.

10. Team and Development Process

Our team consists of three members who collaborated over approximately two months to develop Survive on Moon.

  • Yunus: Game development and programming.
  • Aisha: Game development and programming.
  • Temirlan: UI/UX design and interface development.

During development, we focused on combining scientific research, technical implementation, game design, and educational content into one cohesive experience.

We aimed to create more than just a space-themed game. We wanted to build an interactive educational environment that demonstrates the real challenges of establishing and maintaining human life beyond Earth.

11. Our Vision

Our vision is to transform space education from something children simply read about into something they can experience themselves.

Through Survive on Moon, children become part of an international astronaut crew, face realistic survival challenges, explore the lunar environment, and discover the science behind future space exploration.

We believe the best way to understand the challenges of living on another world is to experience them. Our mission is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers — one lunar mission at a time.
